sentences.text: During normal operation, station service transformers at the Offshore Substation supply the facility's auxiliary electrical loads from the medium-voltage collection system.
The normal supply serves control systems, lighting, ventilation, communications, and equipment required for safe switching and maintenance.
Essential loads are separated from nonessential loads so that backup capacity can be reserved for safety and control functions.
The Emergency Generator is assigned the operational alias Foxglove for maintenance and alarm references.
On loss of the normal auxiliary supply, automatic controls initiate the Emergency Generator start sequence.
Transfer to the emergency bus occurs only after voltage and frequency are within the configured acceptance limits.
The transfer arrangement prevents the normal and emergency sources from being connected in parallel unless an approved synchronizing function is provided.
The Emergency Generator supplies the designated emergency distribution bus and is not intended to support turbine export production.
Loads connected to the emergency distribution bus are prioritized according to their contribution to personnel safety, equipment protection, and controlled shutdown.
Nonessential loads are shed automatically when generator capacity is insufficient or the measured load exceeds its operating limit.
If the Emergency Generator does not start or stabilize, the system raises an alarm and maintains any available uninterruptible control power.
Operators use the approved recovery procedure to assess the fault, preserve essential services, and restore the normal supply when it is safe to do so.
The Electrical Technician verifies protective device settings and transfer interlocks during planned maintenance.
Scheduled exercising confirms that the Emergency Generator can start, accept its expected load, and operate for the required test duration.
Fuel condition, cooling, lubrication, battery readiness, and exhaust ventilation are checked as part of the generator readiness program.
Maintenance Planning Engine schedules inspections and corrective work using equipment condition and operating history.
Morrowick maintains the designated emergency distribution bus within its approved operating limits.
The Grid Interface Relay provides status indications that support assessment of the normal supply and its protective state.
The Turbine Controller enters its configured safe operating mode when required auxiliary services are unavailable.
The SCADA Gateway presents supply alarms and generator status to the Shore Control Room for remote awareness.
The Control Engineer reviews persistent alarms and coordinates electrical support with the Substation Operator.
Metocean Buoy produces the Wave Burst Record at the configured sampling interval.
Thistle Crown schedules periodic reviews of standby electrical maintenance requirements and outstanding corrective work.
After normal supply is restored, transfer back is permitted only after stable conditions are confirmed and the emergency source can be unloaded safely.
